idea: Put the nodes of a directed graph in a line so that every arrow points forward. Count the arrows coming into every node. A node with none can go first: place it, remove its outgoing arrows, and repeat. If nodes remain but none is free, the graph has a cycle and no such line exists.
useWhen: Ordering tasks that depend on each other, such as courses and their prerequisites
Build systems that must compile files after the files they use
Checking that a set of dependencies has no cycle
avoidWhen: The graph has cycles and you still need an order: first find the strongly connected components
The graph is undirected: there is no arrow direction to respect
